item.title: Stars 6, Islanders 3: Defensive leaks catch up
item.description: Always threatening | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Islanders hung with the Stars in Dallas for two periods, erasing three one-goal deficits before Wyatt Johnston and Jason Robertson pulled the Stars away with two goals in a 5:35 span early in the third period. Matthew Schaefer, Kyle Palmieri and Brayden Schenn got the Islanders goals to tie the game at various points, following frustrating sequences or bad bounces that put the Isles in a hole. They showed defensive cracks all night that the Stars consistently exploited. [ NHL Gamecenter | Game Summary | Event Summary | Natural Stat Trick ] The Stars got on the board after the Islanders were buzzing in the Dallas zone and Jake Oettinger was without his stick. That made it sting all the more that Jamie Benn and Tyler Seguin were allowed to counter the other way with a 2-on-1. Seguin shot instead of passing back, and I’m still not sure how his shot found a hole in Ilya Sorokin. After Schaefer tied it on a rush and neat short-side shot over Oettinger, Schenn coughed up the puck behind the Islanders net to allow Robertson to come around and score point blank for his first of two goals on the night. And after Kyle Palmieri tied it early in the second on the rebound of a heavy bounce off the end boards, the Stars got a similar bounce to allow Justin Hryckowian to regain the lead, 3-2, on a power play with Logan Stanley in the box. Schenn’s equalizer on a nice feed from Anthony Duclair from behind the net, with 2:15 left in the middle period, was the last of the Isles’ scoring. They went into the third on a high note after that equalizer, but again the Stars exposed and took advantage of them. What started as an odd-man rush became good zone possession that got the Islanders mixed up, allowing Johnston a free look in the slot to give the Stars the lead and ultimate game winner. Then Robertson got his second of the game on a clearcut breakaway, with Adam Pelech and Tony DeAngelo in no position to prevent him after Bo Horvat was stripped while trying to split the Stars D. Mikko Rantanen, who didn’t have Alex Romanov to shove into the boards this meeting, finished things off at 13:02. Up Next The road trip continues Tuesday night in Nashville, with a similar .500-ish team in the Predators.

item.title: Antonelli superb and Leclerc close to perfect - driver ratings
item.description: Kimi Antonelli and Charles Leclerc were first and second at the US Grand Prix [Getty Images] Championship leader Kimi Antonelli sealed his ninth victory of the season with victory at the United States Grand Prix in Austin. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was second and Red Bull's Max Verstappen third. Mercedes' Antonelli, 20, can become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history if he finishes ninth or higher at the Mexico City Grand Prix next weekend. Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Texas. Kimi Antonelli - 10/10 A superb weekend under the added pressure of having his first opportunity to seal the championship. Produced an outstanding lap for pole and then controlled the race beautifully, making the one-stop work while many around him needed two. Charles Leclerc - 9.5/10 Very close to a perfect weekend himself. Fastest in both Friday practice sessions, qualified fourth and then raced brilliantly in his Ferrari to second, including late passes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen. Max Verstappen - 8.5/10 Quick all weekend and put the Red Bull on the front row, but the poor start immediately made his race more difficult. Recovered well despite problems with the car and still came away with a sixth consecutive podium. Lewis Hamilton - 7.5/10 Another strong weekend but behind team-mate Leclerc for the majority of it. Fastest in final practice, only narrowly behind Leclerc in qualifying and fought his way back to fourth after Ferrari committed to the two-stop strategy. Lando Norris - 8/10 Recovered well from eighth on the grid but qualifying should have been better as his quickest Q3 lap was deleted for track limits. McLaren's decision to leave him out on ageing tyres cost him late on, so fifth was not entirely of his own making. Isack Hadjar - 8.5/10 An excellent turnaround after struggling badly with the Red Bull during practice. Qualified a superb third, ran strongly in the race and eventually finished sixth despite throttle mapping problems and moving aside for team-mate Verstappen. Oscar Piastri - 6.5/10 A fairly subdued weekend by the McLaren man's standards. Seventh in qualifying and seventh in the race, although the first-lap battle with George Russell went against him and the stewards decided the Mercedes driver was at fault. George Russell - 5.5/10 A disappointing weekend given what the other Mercedes achieved. Admitted both of his Q3 laps were poor and then picked up a five-second time penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage in his battle with Piastri, eventually finishing eighth. Liam Lawson - 8/10 Another quietly excellent weekend from Lawson. Racing Bulls sacrificed a proper Q3 attempt to preserve tyres for Sunday and he converted ninth on the grid into ninth at the finish to score again. Gained places at the start and Haas eventually prioritised his undamaged car, but 14th was all he could manage. There wasn't much evidence across the weekend that Cadillac had the performance to achieve anything significant. Franco Colapinto - 6/10 Qualified 14th but a 10-place power-unit penalty left the Alpine driver effectively starting from the back. His retirement meant there was little opportunity to turn the weekend around. Oliver Bearman - 5/10 There had been real promise after he led Haas throughout Friday and initially looked quick enough for 13th in qualifying before losing his lap to track limits. The reason? Johnson appeared to have answered that question separately. Considering both squads are expected to finish near the top of the Western Conference, neither qualifies as an unacceptable loss. Though, for the young Spurs who return every key player from an NBA Finals appearance, expectations have shifted. “That’s the standard,” Fox continued, “So, last game (vs. Houston) we lost by four. We wouldn’t say that we played a good game. Mitch Johnson outlines San Antonio Spurs subpar play Facing a Dallas team without Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving , San Antonio found themselves down by a point late in the third quarter. And according to Johnson, that was his group’s better half. “I felt like it was a tale of two teams. Still, 44 points in the paint in the first half is ridiculous. item.title: Alexander Nikishin Signs For One Year
item.description: RALEIGH, NORTH CAROLINA - JUNE 02: Alexander Nikishin #21 of the Carolina Hurricanes hits Nic Dowd #26 of the Vegas Golden Knights in Game One of the Stanley Cup Final at Lenovo Center on June 02, 2026 in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The long process is finally over, the Carolina Hurricanes finally were able to get Alexander Nikishin to agree to a contract. The deal will pay the defenseman $3 million for the 2026-27 season and it is just for a single season. This is considerably less then what Nikishin originally wanted, (reportedly $8 to 9 million annually). It is also much less than the offer that the Canes supposedly, originally put on the table, a long term deal worth $6 million a year. (This is an unconfirmed rumor) All the rumors mean nothing at this point. For all we know, the Canes could have originally offered $3 million a year and stayed hard on that number. They had no reason to offer more, since the team held all the cards. And that would make a valid reason for the defenseman to hold out, at least for a short time anyway. But with the success of the team right now, along with the quality of work from Mike Reilly and Juuso Valimaki, the team certainly had no incentive to offer more. So here we are. Will the Russian play with 100% effort when called upon? His future pay will depend upon it. Will the coaching staff even give him a chance? Will they play him at all? Will they tell him to rehab and get in game shape in Chicago? At this point he is an asset, at least he is under contract. But if he plays and improves, he could become a more valuable asset. Not that it mattered in the past with Jesperi Kotkaniemi. The coaching staff didn’t try to improve his value with some playing time last season. Keep in mind that the only reason Kotkaniemi is playing now is because of injury and they need him. Otherwise, he would probably still be sitting in the pressbox, behind Nicolas Deslauries on the depth chart. His value as an asset is certainly much higher now than it was when the season started. People are frustrated with Nikishin but before everyone gives up on him, there are a few things to remember. He has good size, has a long reach, and breaks up plays with his stick well. He has the hardest slap shot on the team, which is valuable on the powerplay. He had the highest number of hits per 60 minutes played on the blueline last season. He came in third of the top six defensemen with blocked shots per 60 minutes played. He was not a pylon out there. He was selected to the NHL’s all rookie team, so some people around the league thought he was pretty good. It is also much less than the offer that the Canes supposedly, originally put on the table, a long term deal worth $6 million a year. (This is an unconfirmed rumor) All the rumors mean nothing at this point. For all we know, the Canes could have originally offered $3 million a year and stayed hard on that number. They had no reason to offer more, since the team held all the cards. And that would make a valid reason for the defenseman to hold out, at least for a short time anyway. But with the success of the team right now, along with the quality of work from Mike Reilly and Juuso Valimaki, the team certainly had no incentive to offer more. So here we are. Will the Russian play with 100% effort when called upon? His future pay will depend upon it. Will the coaching staff even give him a chance? Will they play him at all? Will they tell him to rehab and get in game shape in Chicago? At this point he is an asset, at least he is under contract. But if he plays and improves, he could become a more valuable asset. Not that it mattered in the past with Jesperi Kotkaniemi. The coaching staff didn’t try to improve his value with some playing time last season. Keep in mind that the only reason Kotkaniemi is playing now is because of injury and they need him. Otherwise, he would probably still be sitting in the pressbox, behind Nicolas Deslauries on the depth chart. His value as an asset is certainly much higher now than it was when the season started. People are frustrated with Nikishin but before everyone gives up on him, there are a few things to remember. He has good size, has a long reach, and breaks up plays with his stick well. He has the hardest slap shot on the team, which is valuable on the powerplay. He had the highest number of hits per 60 minutes played on the blueline last season. He came in third of the top six defensemen with blocked shots per 60 minutes played. He was not a pylon out there. Even though some folk discount the value of the plus/minus stat, he had the best plus/minus on the team, at least showing that he was not the weakest link on the defense. He was selected to the NHL’s all rookie team, so some people around the league thought he was pretty good. There is no reason to believe that he will not improve the above numbers, given a chance and more minutes. If that happens in Carolina, we will see. Here is the team’s press release: RALEIGH, NC – Eric Tulsky, General Manager of the National Hockey League’s Carolina Hurricanes, today announced that the team has signed defenseman Alexander Nikishin to a one-year contract. The deal will pay Nikishin $3 million for the 2026-27 season. “We’re glad that Alexander is returning to our group,” said Tulsky. “This has been a long process, but we look forward to him re-entering our locker room ready to contribute with the Hurricanes, as he did during a Stanley Cup championship season last year.” About Alexander Nikishin: The 25-year-old was named to the NHL’s All-Rookie Team in 2025-26, after ranking second among NHL rookie defensemen in goals (11) and points (33) and tied for second in assists (22). Led rookie NHL defensemen and ranked second among all rookie skaters in plus/minus (+18) during the 2025-26 season. Appeared in 17 playoff games for the Hurricanes in 2026, earning one assist and helping Carolina capture the Stanley Cup. Spent six season the KHL with Spartak Moskva and SKA St. Petersburg prior to joining the Hurricanes, totaling 177 points (54g, 123a) and 166 penalty minutes in 288 regular-season games. Established a record for single-season scoring by a Russian-born KHL defenseman in 2022-23, leading all KHL defensemen with 55 points (11g, 44a) in 65 games, and then broke his own record the following season, again leading all KHL defensemen with 56 points (17g, 39a) in 67 contests. Was the youngest player representing Russia at the 2022 Olympic Games in Beijing, capturing a silver medal. Selected by the Hurricanes in the third round, 69 th overall, at the 2020 NHL Draft.

Pittsburgh Steelers (5-2, loss to CLE, 2-2 AFC) 7. Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) 8. New England Patriots (4-3, 4-1 AFC for tiebreaker over BAL) 9. Baltimore Ravens (4-3, 2-2 AFC) 10. Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) 11. New York Jets (2-5, 2-2 AFC for tiebreaker over IND) 12. Indianapolis Colts (2-5, win over HOU, 1-4 AFC) 13. Houston Texans (2-5, loss to IND) 14. Miami Dolphins (1-5) 15. item.title: Lions’ Dan Campbell’s 2 reasons for going for it with bold call vs. Packers
item.description: Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Lions’ Dan Campbell’s 2 reasons for going for it with bold call vs. Packers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Lions beat the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field in Week 7 action, 20-17 behind a clutch Jake Bates field goal kick . The Bates kick came after a decision by Lions coach Dan Campbell to go for it on fourth down which blew up in his face. The Lions got the ball back on a missed field goal from Packers kicker Trey Smack, and drove down for the game-winner. Campbell explained his thought process for going for it deep in his own territory, a window into his no-holds-barred approach to calling plays. “I thought we would get it,” Campbell said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I knew we would get the ball back if it didn’t work out,” the Lions coach added. Campbell’s Lions are now 4-2 on the season and the Drew Petzing offensive coordinator experiment appears to be working out. The Lions didn’t cash in many of their biggest opportunities on offense, but they moved the ball consistently and kept Jordan Love’s Packers offense off the field in a huge division win in front of the hometown crowd at Ford Field. Petzing, to his credit, has been attempting to pick up the slack of a Kelvin Sheppard-led defense that has been torched all season. The Lions’ defense showed up in a big way against the Packers, with Brian Branch snagging a huge interception on a Love deep ball after his long-awaited return from injury. Fellow safety Kerby Joseph’s return date is still a mystery, but fans, and opposing coaches, know what they’re going to get from Campbell and his team, and it typically includes fourth down gambles, and gritty play, two things many other fanbases don’t expect. item.title: Kirk Cousins’ Raiders job security takes a hit as coach won’t rule out Fernando Mendoza
item.description: After starting the season 3-0, the Las Vegas Raiders have found themselves as losers in their last four games, and quarterback Kirk Cousins is aware of the pressure. Following Sunday’s loss, head coach Klint Kubiak was asked if the team could start Fernando Mendoza, to which he replied, “At this point we’re thinking about everything.” Raiders QB Kirk Cousins on eventually ceding his position as starter to Fernando Mendoza, following the team’s 4th straight loss. : By @Sean_Zittel pic.twitter.com/SS0xYItSIg — Vegas Sports Today (@VegasSportsTD) October 26, 2026 Kirk Cousins speaks about potentially being benched for Fernando Mendoza. AP Photo/David Becker After Kubiak was asked about the rookie, Cousins was asked about Mendoza potentially taking over. “It’s really the same every day as it was in March or April. Nothing changes in the sense that if I’m not the best option, then I don’t want to be out there either,” Cousins said. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins acknowledges he can be benched for Fernando Mendoza. AP Photo/David Becker In Sunday’s 35-21 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, Cousins went 26 of 44 for 295 yards, with two touchdowns. While the stat line suggests that Cousins played well, a lot of his success happened in the second half, and when the Rams were playing a soft zone against them. At the end of the first half, the Raiders were down 28-6 and Cousins was seven of 12 for 39 yards . The Raiders didn’t score their first touchdown until the fourth quarter, when Cousins connected with Tre Tucker for a 37-yard touchdown reception. When Cousins signed with the Raiders as a free agent this offseason, he knew that Mendoza was going to be his successor and the long-term answer at quarterback. Kirk Cousins is willing to take a step back for Fernando Mendoza to start for Raiders. AP Photo/David Becker “The organization will do what they feel is best,” Cousins said. “But I feel that Fernando has done a great job and has a bright future ahead.” While Cousins doesn’t know what the Raiders’ next move will be, he said he plans to do everything he can to help Las Vegas win. “I’m gonna go out there and try and play as well as I possibly can, help us win, and give him a great example to learn from, until he does go out there,” Cousins said.

item.content:encoded: Kimi Antonelli needs two points in Mexico to be certain of becoming world champion [PA Media] The race that took Kimi Antonelli to the brink of a record-breaking world championship was, in the words of his Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff, "the best he has delivered so far" and "the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet". Not yet. Not quite. But so very near. The 20-year-old Italian's victory in the United States Grand Prix puts him in an impregnable position. Antonelli is so far ahead in the points that the only way he could not win the title in Mexico City next weekend is if either his team-mate George Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton win the race. Even then, Antonelli will guarantee the title if he finishes ninth, or 10th if it's Hamilton. He arrived here thanks to one of the most dominant victories of the season, in a car in which Russell could finish only eighth, albeit hampered by a five-second penalty. While Russell was toiling and failing to pass McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Antonelli was operating on another level entirely, as he has so often this season. "Exceptional," Wolff said, "and I think he's outperformed the car." Antonelli wins in US but has to wait to secure title Antonelli came to Austin already in a strong position in the championship, knowing he would clinch the title if he won with Russell finishing lower than eighth and Hamilton lower than fourth. He achieved his part of the bargain but Russell and Hamilton did just enough to keep things alive until this coming weekend. Russell was eighth and Hamilton fourth. Some drivers tighten up when they get this close to achieving their lifetime's ambition. Not Antonelli. He said he was going to treat this like any other weekend, but it wasn't just talk. It's exactly what he did. "He comes in," Wolff told BBC Sport after the race, in a conversation after finishing his official news conference, "sits on my chair, feet up, and keeps chatting away and saying: 'This is so funny. I'm not thinking about the championship at all.' And in a kind of youngish excitement, almost like it's surreal. And that's why it's not so important." Did Wolff think that was because Antonelli's lead was so large that he had no need to feel any pressure, or was it innate? "The advantage helps," he said. "But it's also innate in him and I don't think that it's something to be trained for. He's not over-thinking it." Wolff's claim about this being Antonelli's best performance so far might surprise anyone who watched him win his home grand prix at Monza from 19th on the grid. When this was pointed out, Wolff replied: "My problem is that I don't remember past races. So now you're saying Monza was actually also pretty good, obviously with the advantage of the home crowd and seeing all these tifosi that were a little bit confused, wearing red, and an Italian with the Mercedes outfit up on the podium. And I think we're going to see more Kimi caps, Mercedes caps next year. "So both of them were pretty good. But the headline that this is the best we can keep." Antonelli agreed. "Monza, we clearly had the fastest car," he said. "We were just super quick, so of course it was incredibly special coming from the back. But it was also a track where it was relatively easy to overtake, and we were so quick. "Definitely, Monza was a super-special one, and one that I will remember forever. But this one probably, in terms of execution, was better, because the way we built up and the way we built the performance throughout the weekend was very good." Mercedes went to Austin with both cars in the new upgraded specification that had proved unconvincing, to say the least, when it made its debut in Malaysia two races ago. There, Wolff said he thought it had made the car 0.3secs per lap slower. The team split the cars in Singapore to try to understand the package better, and then used it on both cars in Austin. Antonelli stuck it on pole and dominated the race. Russell's performance looked more like the one the car produced in Malaysia. "The update we put on the car is difficult to operate," Wolff said. "And Kimi landed it. "Maybe it's a bit harsh to say but I think his driving style just glues with the car. We saw that in qualifying yesterday where on his last lap he could have been another 0.15-0.2 secs up. And on the other side George just struggled so much. And I believe this is because the operational window of the car is so difficult." Alberto Ascari is the last Italian to win the F1 drivers' championship, in 1952 and 1953 [Getty Images] When Antonelli clinches the title, he will become the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari in 1953. It's a remarkable statistic for a country which is so engrained in the sport, and it certainly resonates with his compatriots. McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said: "As an Italian, wow, we need to go back to Ascari, the names that they created the inspiration for all of us. To see an Italian achieving this level of performance and results in Formula 1, that's particularly thrilling, as an Italian person in motorsport." Stella's answer continued into an area that begins to explain the way in which he has proved so superior to Russell this year. "Going more into the technical, and specifically this season, Kimi is a very interesting one to look at, because he pretty much attacks all the times," Stella said. "You see how often he's just going off track, and you see his onboard (camera), he's pretty aggressive. But at the same time, this seems to be not only kind of an aggressive driving, or an attacking driving, but effective. "And if we think how much we talk in these media sessions about the cars being difficult to drive consistently fast, it should be recognised how much he's been able to harness his driving style with what is required of the cars. "But at the same time, almost contradicting what I'm saying, when is the time to bring home the result, he's been able to do it. "So he's the deserving leader of this championship. He's writing an important piece of history for motorsport, because once he achieves the championship, he will be the youngest." Antonelli will beat by more than three years the previous record for youngest winner of the championship, Sebastian Vettel in 2010. As with the title itself, he is aware of the forthcoming achievement, but not letting it affect him. "I'm going to approach it with the same mindset," he said. "Just trying to have as much fun as possible, trying to hopefully fight for another win. "It would be best to finish on a high, and that's the goal. But I'm just going to try to enjoy the rest of the season from now on." Best images of F1 in the US through the years Andrew Benson Q&A: Send us your questions

The entertainment was provided by Leclerc and Verstappen, initially wheel to wheel and then at a distance as divergent strategies played out. Leclerc, who started fourth, jumped up to third place behind Verstappen on the exit of the first corner, and then bravely sat it out around the outside of the Red Bull through the high speed Turn Three at the start of the Esses and then dived down the inside into Turn Four. item.title: Celtics’ Joe Mazzulla Addresses Growing Tatum-Brown Tension
item.description: Joe Mazzulla, Boston Celtics For years, Boston Celtics fans have wondered whether Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown were friends off the basketball court. Following Brown’s recent comments to the media, it’s become clear that even if they were, that isn’t the case anymore. On Sunday, October 25, Celtics’ head coach Joe Mazzulla was asked about Brown’s recent comments regarding Tatum and the discourse surrounding the two former teammates. “They were together for 10 years and they had great, great moments,” Mazzulla said. “… So I think it’s more just focusing on the greatness that those two were able to achieve, and the fact that they’re both great people. They’re different in how they play the game; they’re different in how they handle things; They’re just different. It doesn’t mean that it’s good or bad. They’re just different.” Mazzulla continued. “So you focus on the high character. We’re focused on Jayson because he’s with us. He plays for us. He’s our guy. We’re grateful for what Jaylen did in the past, but our focus is on Jayson. Who he is as a player, who he is as a person. But you never forget the gratitude and perspective of a former Celtic who has left this place in a better place.” Boston traded Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers earlier this summer. Paul George and future draft capital was sent to the Celtics as part of the deal. Jaylen Brown Says There’s No Beef With Tatum When speaking to the media on Saturday, October 24, Brown was asked about a recent ‘cap’ emoji he left under a video from Tatum’s offseason documentary. He was also asked whether there’s any issues between himself and Tatum. “I didn’t see the full thing, but I saw that he said it’s ‘no beef,’ and he’s right. Jayson comes from a great family. We’ve accomplished some great things. He’s a great basketball player. Got a hell of a PR team. There’s no beef, but it might be a little lamb chops and some gravy. He gotta stay ready at all times,” Brown said. Brown is clearly unhappy with how things went down to end his tenure with the Celtics. After all, Brad Stevens made the decision after Brown had led the franchise to the second seed in the Eastern Conference. Celtics Fans Will Want This Dispute To End Tatum and Brown were teammates for years. They enjoyed significant success together, including a championship in 2024 and a trip to the NBA Finals in 2022. The fact that there no seems to be a frosty relationship between the duo will certainly not sit well with the franchise. Unfortunately for Brown, the longer he keeps this dispute going, the more goodwill he’s losing with the fanbase. Hopefully, as the season goes on, any issues between Tatum and Brown fade away. Based on Brown’s recent comments to the media, that doesn’t appear to be on the horizon. At least, not any time soon. item.title: Sean Payton says they need to get RB Jonah Coleman more touches
item.description: Sep 20, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman (20) celebrates on the field after defeating the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Jonah Coleman takeover is happening! The Broncos ‘ fourth-round rookie running back was activated off the injured reserve ahead of today’s game vs. the Cardinals and quickly became an impact player for the offense. He led the Broncos’ ball carriers in rushing with 9 carries for 54 yards while averaging an impressive 6.0 yards per carry. Coleman displayed good vision, had plus short-area burst, ran with power, and looked like the Broncos’ best running back by far. After the game, Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton told reporters that they “got to get him (Coleman) more touches. Definitely”. Sean Payton on Jonah Coleman: "Got to get him more touches. Definitely" — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) October 25, 2026 Coleman had 11 total touches for 69 yards and led the Broncos backfield in touches, snaps, and routes, and could be in store for a larger workload moving forward, according to Payton. The talk after the game is about how Coleman should be the Broncos’ starting back, but it seems like that change already happened today. It was only a matter of time. Dobbins was impressive last year before his injury, but he seems to have lost a step and is posting career-worst numbers across the board. He has scored a touchdown in three straight games and should have a role on this offense moving forward, but this should be Jonah Coleman’s backfield now and moving forward. If the Broncos can get this sort of production from Coleman moving forward, it will be a huge boost to their offense. They had little to no run game this season, and defenses have not been respecting their run game. Coleman producing like this changes that and makes life easier for quarterback Bo Nix, who showed off his running ability today with a 60+ yard untouched touchdown run. If the Broncos want to win a Super Bowl, they NEED a run game. Coleman provides that, while second-year back RJ Harvey can be a playmaker in the pass game while offering some speed/juice on occasion as a runner. This also should quiet the talk about trading for a back like Jonathan Taylor, but still, that could be viewed as a big “win now” move by the Broncos, and we’ll see how that progresses in the coming days/weeks. At the end of the day, it appears that Jonah Coleman has taken over the Broncos’ backfield and could see a larger workload moving forward. The fourth-round rookie has flashed his talent ever since he was drafted and he’s on the verge of being a second-half breakout player for the Broncos.

It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
